target.purpose: Test five unused exact-track hypotheses after a fresh current-release, adjacent-label and overlooked-catalogue scan. Character changes are allowed; admission still requires purposeful transition, local-run and long-form effect.

sourceWindows: CURRENT / KRUNCHTIME: https://kuttinedge.bandcamp.com/track/fix-the-news — Kuttin Edge's August 12, 2026 Fix The News and surrounding current catalogue were screened. The exact page provides identity and packaging but no track-level rhythmic or structural account, so it remains a release watch rather than a ranked lead.

CURRENT / RESIDENT ADVISOR: https://ra.co/reviews and https://ra.co/features/4490 — the September 3, 2026 August roundup and current review index were screened. Previously retained Picture, Reptant, FAUZIA, RHR, Answer Code Request and Exhale identities were excluded.

ADJACENT / CLASICO AND LOCAL ACTION: https://ra.co/reviews/35465 — all four Coffintexts Touch tracks were screened. Toxic was retained from the exact review's chest-rattling subs and start-stop rhythm.

ADJACENT / TRA TRA TRAX: https://ra.co/reviews/35339 — all five versions on Tomás Urquieta's 32 Balas package were screened. The title track was retained from its exact account of non-synchronous elements and drums dropping in and out.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / HOSPITAL PRODUCTIONS: https://ra.co/reviews/19982 — all ten Shifted Appropriation Stories tracks were screened. Flatlands was retained from the exact review's loose-ball-bearing motif moving around a motoring rhythm section.
ADJACENT / JUNGLE FANTASY: https://ra.co/reviews/35823 — Chloé Robinson & DJ ADHD's Do One EP was screened. 0121 Do One was retained from its exact syncopated snare-and-kick pattern.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / RITUAL POISON: https://ra.co/reviews/33753 — Witch Trials' Hollow Grave package was screened. The title track was retained from the exact description of broken techno overtaken by synth fog and crescendo.

ADDITIONAL WINDOWS: UMFANG's 1080p catalogue, Seph/Insurgentes, Nkisi/UIQ and current Bandcamp electronic indexes were screened. Release-level claims and already-preserved Run 53–77 identities stayed below the ranked list.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 43 named tracks and releases across current releases, adjacent and emerging artists and labels, and overlooked catalogue windows; metadata and attributed descriptions only, with zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 14 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Exact identities and primary discovery lanes retained in Runs 53–77 were not recycled.
The protected internal handoffs Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and every other boundary remain available.
No lead was promoted for recency, reputation, genre, novelty, title or technical cleverness. Release-level claims were not converted into exact-track behavior.

Energy, density, space, hypnosis, emotional effect, phrase structure, harmonic relation, perceived pulse and mixability remain unknown. Descriptions of syncopation, broken rhythm and structural change are evidence, not flow verdicts.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Tomás Urquieta — 32 Balas: strongest exact internal-dislocation account, with elements out of time and drums dropping in and out.
2. Coffintexts — Toxic: strongest adjacent start-stop construction, with exact-track subs and interrupted rhythm.
3. Shifted — Flatlands: strongest overlooked polyrhythmic-gait lead, with a spatially mobile motif over a motoring rhythm section.
4. Chloé Robinson & DJ ADHD — 0121 Do One: strongest compact syncopated-kick-and-snare lead.
5. Witch Trials — Hollow Grave: strongest full-form transformation, from broken techno into synth fog and crescendo.
